walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 1: Guided Literary Analysis — a core area of English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 1: Guided Literary Analysis brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 1: Guided Literary Analysis.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term ostranenie (defamiliarisation) in 1917?
options: Viktor Shklovsky
Roman Jakobson
Boris Eikhenbaum
Yuri Tynyanov

mcqs.q: Whose 1946 essay attacked the intentional fallacy?
options: Wimsatt and Beardsley
Brooks and Warren
Frye and Bloom
Empson and Richards
Epic means any story with a battle in it.
An unreliable narrator is one who tells lies in the story.
An unreliable narrator is when the author makes mistakes.
Their account is undermined within the text by ignorance, bias, self-deception or deceit, so the reader must read against what they say.

mcqs.q: Why distinguish the speaker of a poem from the poet?
options: The speaker is the voice constructed in the poem; the poet is the writer. Treating them as identical can mislead, especially with dramatic monologues or personae.
The speaker is whoever reads the poem out loud.
Epic means any story with a battle in it.
The speaker of a poem is always the poet themselves.

mcqs.q: What defines epic poetry as a genre?
options: An unreliable narrator is when the author makes mistakes.
Epic means any poem that is very long.
Epic means any story with a battle in it.
Long narrative poems on heroic subjects, in elevated style, often invoking a muse, in medias res openings, and treating events of national or cosmic significance.
